segments.text: A dairy line running 24 hours a day throws off far more downtime events than any manual form can keep up with. Every micro-stop — a jam, a changeover, a sensor fault — needed its own entry: start time, stop time, reason, type. Multiply that across machines and shifts, and operators were spending more time filling downtime forms than running the line.
CT sensors already know when a machine stopped and started. What they can’t capture is why, or what was made, so for every segment on the timeline the operator logs:

items.text: — the production entry: SKU, batch order and quantity produced.

segments.text: The first fix was a visual one: a color-coded timeline per machine, one bar per day, segments colored by downtime type. It solved the volume problem at a glance — utilization and availability were visible instantly. But it created a new one.

Packed into a single bar, individual micro-stops were too small and too close together to tell apart, let alone tap accurately. Operators could see that something had gone wrong, but not which segment it was or how to log it.

items.caption: Before — every micro-stop had to be found on a crowded bar and tapped one at a time to log its reason.
Before — the reason dropdown overflowed its pop-up, so operators had to close it before they could save.

segments.text: PatternLab's Factory Intelligence pulls machine state from CT sensors on the line, cleans and organizes it, and puts it in front of operators to fill the forms:

items.text: — Utilization (%) and Availability (%) per machine, with uptime, downtime, Clean in progress (CIP), deviation segments color-coded across the day, for a one-glance read on how a machine is doing.

— the three-dot menu on any machine breaks its timeline into a structured list: one row per downtime event, with start time, stop time, duration, and a reason dropdown, laid out the same way whether there are three stops that shift or thirty.
— resting on any segment surfaces exactly what it is: start time, end time, duration, reason (if logged). No more guessing which sliver of color is which stop.

items.caption: After — utilisation and availability sit beside each machine’s timeline for a one-glance read.
After — the three-dot menu expands a machine into a structured downtime list: one row per stop, one reason dropdown each.
After — the selected segment is highlighted on the bar, so it’s always clear which stop is being logged.
After — uptime opens the Production form (SKU, batch order, quantity) in the same view as downtime, lab tests and yield.

segments.text: Downtime capture sits alongside Production, Lab Test, and Yield forms in the same view, so the operator isn't switching screens to reconstruct what happened on a line.
, so the timeline, the forms and the rest of the product share one set of components.

segments.text: Previously, filling in reasons for every micro-stop meant tapping into each segment individually, and the pop-up dropdown often didn't fit the screen, requiring scrolling — making the flow overwhelming.

This has been simplified: tapping any segment (uptime, downtime, or other) now shows all downtime segments at once, letting the operator fill in reasons immediately. The relevant bar segment also highlights, so it’s always clear which segment the reason is being entered for.
